$Comment: The Mastery Trainer, standing in the Forgotten Temple across from the Adventurer's Guide.
The trainer is this pack's character end to end: their look, their role, this placement, and
the conversation pressing F opens all ship here, so a server without the pack has no trainer
to stand up. Interact names a conversation rather than a screen, because the trainer has
quests to hand out and a word to say before the mastery menu; a screen name there would open
the menu with no conversation at all. Author Open or Dialogue, never both.
To take the trainer out without editing this file, set Enabled false in
mods/ziggfreedcommon/npc-placements.json.
Where targets the temple by its GameplayConfig key rather than by name: that key is the
engine's own per-world gameplay-config id - 'ForgottenTemple' ships with the base game - and
it is the same every time the temple is entered, while the world NAME carries a fresh uuid
each time.
Requires keeps the trainer away until the mastery feature is switched on; Lifecycle keeps
their chunk loaded, puts them back if something removes them, and raises their health beyond
anything that can be dealt. This placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS its
role: the pack's mastery quests bind to Mmo_Mastery_Trainer, and any second placement of that
role is the same trainer, offering and taking hand-ins for the same quests.
The trainer stands beside the temple's own Rootling Merchant spawn marker rather than at the
raw portal-landing point, so moving with the temple's actual layout instead of an offset that
can land inside a wall. To move them, edit Anchor.Structure.Offset, keeping it small enough to
stay out of the walls.
Name: Mmo_Mastery_Trainer_Temple
